searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's. The appellation search and the Negoska search on winesofgreece.org are counted with Aidarinis. Four were restricted to a body's own domain (winesofgreece.org twice, boutari.gr twice) and read as primary for that body's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on no source was cut; a claim of a house about itself was hedged as its account.

appellation.tested: PDO Goumenissa of 1979 on the south eastern foothills of Mount Paiko in Kilkis, Xinomavro with at least 20 per cent Negoska; Negoska named from the Slavic Negush for Naoussa and planted almost only on the Paiko slopes: Wines of Greece, its PDO page and its Negoska page (search on its own domain). Every record's appellation lines stand.
appellation.note: One secondary guide says the two grapes must be fermented together; Wines of Greece does not say so, and the records rightly leave it out.

tested: The family in Goumenissa since the late nineteenth century making wine and tsipouro: a Greek tour operator (late nineteenth century, tsipouro) and two merchants (more than a century, late nineteenth century); kept as merchants' accounts.
1978: the winery in its present form by one merchant, the first vineyard in rows by another; founded stays empty, the story gives both.

Vineyards south of the town on the eastern slopes of Paiko at 200 to 250 metres, grapes bought from growers of the zone: a merchant's profile and a Greek Master of Wine's note of 250 metres for the single vineyard; kept.
Twelve months in oak for the Goumenissa (2019 by two merchants, French by one); the Single Vineyard twelve months in new French oak and six in bottle (Botilia's 2017 sheet); kept.
The Single Vineyard planted in 1978 as a field blend (a London critic's note) on a parcel of about 250 metres; the blend given as 60 to 40 and 70 to 30 in different vintages, so no share is printed.

open: Boutari and Wines of Greece call the Boutari winery of 1984 the only one in the area for many years, while merchants date the Aidarinis winery to 1978: the tension is reported, both kept as accounts.
French oak for the plain Goumenissa rests on one merchant.

tested: The founder an engineer who made wine as a hobby and married a woman of Goumenissa: a British importer's profile, a Greek foundation's profile and a merchant agree (mechanical engineer in two, electrical in one, so only engineer is printed).

The first vineyard of 1994 at Bindabla, farmed organically from the start: the wine glossary, a merchant's listing and the importer agree; the winery at Filyria built in 2007 by one account only, left undated as the author did.

Seven parts Xinomavro to three of Negoska, two days of cold soak, eight months on lees, twelve months in French oak with no new oak: the importer's 2020 and 2021 sheets and a merchant; sixteen and eighteen months in other vintages by a Master of Wine's note and a bar's listing; kept as about twelve, longer in some vintages.
miniMus: Xinomavro alone, PGI Slopes of Paiko, wild fermented in steel, four months in French oak: the importer's sheets; kept. Negoska Carbonic and Mosaic Red: a critic's listings and the importer.

changed.why: The spelling of the importer and two estate profiles.

changed.why: The importer's sheets give Roditis in the white blend; Malagousia and Assyrtiko were not found.

tested: Refugees from Ano Vodeno in Eastern Rumelia settled in Goumenissa in 1924: two profiles (a wine tourism directory and a tour operator) in near the same words; kept, now told as the family's account.
Two brothers took over from their father and made their first vintage in 1996: two profiles agree; kept, the father added.
Organic certification in 1998 and biodynamic farming from 2002: three profiles agree; kept, the question stands.

Wild yeasts, nothing added, unfiltered, long élevage and release with bottle age: an American importer's copy and the house's RAW WINE sheet; old oak casks rest on the RAW sheet only, which is the house's own declaration.

tested: The estate at the foot of Paiko among old oaks beside the Sirios, near Dyo Potamia: a Thessaloniki guide, a tour operator and Greek merchants agree; kept.

The founder dead, his widow handing the estate on, and the revival in 2018 by the founders of Ktima Biblia Chora: the guide and the tour operator (the late founder, 2018), a Greek trade publication; kept, the widow still left out.
Four parts Xinomavro to one of Negoska, and a Negoska alone: the guide and the tour operator; kept. Large French casks for about a year: two British merchants, as the author read.

changed.why: Two guides give the estate's opening as the founder's first planting beside the Sirios in 1972; the author had one merchant only.

Both guides may repeat the estate's own text for 1972.

tested: The winery at Goumenissa began in 1984 and was for many years the only winery in the area: Wines of Greece's profile and a Boutari page (search on their own domains); kept, hedged as the house's account.

Domaine Filyria planted in 1991, organic, mostly Xinomavro and Negoska with trials of Chardonnay, Syrah, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, called a model vineyard: the house's Goumenissa page (search on boutari.gr) and Wines of Greece; kept.
Filiria: Xinomavro and Negoska from the house's vineyard at Filyria, at least twelve months in French oak (Allier and Nevers barrels for the 2008): two merchants; kept.
The house founded at Naoussa in 1879: the house's history page and Wines of Greece; kept, the founder still unnamed for want of dates.

changed.was: Smaller family wineries have since grown up around it in the zone, among them Aidarinis, Tatsis and Chatzivaritis.
changed.now: In the 1990s smaller family estates began to bottle their own Goumenissa beside it, Chatzivaritis and Tatsis among them.
changed.why: Merchants date the Aidarinis winery to 1978 and the family to the late nineteenth century, so it did not grow up after Boutari's winery of 1984; Chatzivaritis planted in 1994 and Tatsis made its first vintage in 1996.

changed.was: by the house's own account it was for many years the only winery
changed.now: by the house's own account, which Wines of Greece repeats, it was for many years the only winery
changed.why: Both bodies say it; it stays the house's claim.

open: That Filiria is still bottled is not confirmed: a Cypriot importer lists it in its portfolio, but no vintage after 2008 was found. The integrator should confirm before it ships.
The pick stays in doubt, as the author said: Boutari is also the pick of Naoussa.

swaps.ruling: No swap was proposed by the author, so none is ruled. On the Boutari pick in doubt: kept for now, since the fragment takes the Goumenissa estate wine and never the Naoussa wines, and no sixth producer of the zone stands ready; it is for the merge agent.

questions: All ten questions were read for one right answer, plausible distractors of one kind and a teaching explanation. They stand. The Chatzivaritis story question's distractor of a Naoussa house buying land in the 1980s is near Boutari's history but is wrong for Chatzivaritis, and the explanation says so; the Boutari story question's 1984 rests on the house and Wines of Greece.
codexTension: The region record's producers line for Aidarinis speaks of old vine bottlings; only the Single Vineyard of 1978 vines was found. Reported, not edited.
The region summary calls Goumenissa a district of a few family estates and one large house; Boutari's only winery claim and the Aidarinis date of 1978 sit uneasily together. Reported, not edited.
